name: llm_wiki
description: LLM Wiki is a cross-platform desktop application that turns your documents into an organized, interlinked knowledge base — automatically. Instead of traditional RAG (retrieve-and-answer from scratch every time), the LLM incrementally builds and maintains a persistent wiki from your sources。
one_liner: A desktop app that reads all your documents and automatically organizes them into a linked personal wiki, so you can search and browse your own knowledge instead of digging through folders.
buyer: A PhD researcher or consultant sitting on hundreds of PDFs and notes who needs an organized, browsable knowledge base but doesn't have time to manually file and cross-link everything.
business_use_cases: A research lab standardizes on it to turn shared papers and reports into a browsable team knowledge base instead of a messy shared drive.
A consulting firm builds a persistent client-knowledge wiki from meeting notes and documents that any consultant on the account can search.
A journalist or analyst uses it to organize investigation sources into a linked wiki with source-grounded search for fact-checking.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a hosted team edition with shared wikis and permissions, priced per seat.
Sell a managed cloud sync/backup add-on for the local wiki data.

steal_this: Package a narrow version aimed at one niche (e.g. 'research wiki for PhD students') with a guided onboarding flow and sell it directly to grad students this weekend.
